html:
SMTO-EXE-0054 — SMTO couldn't find that app on the computer

GUID: a7fc633b-70f8-5f1d-be25-59fb9d5d8d2d
Slug: desktop-application-not-found
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: desktop

What happened

  • SMTO looked for the app you asked it to open on the Gateway computer but couldn't find it there, so nothing was started.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Check that the app is installed on the Gateway computer you selected, not only on the computer you're using. SMTO opens apps on the selected Gateway computer, which may be a different machine.
  2. Give SMTO the app's full location on that computer, for example C:\Program Files\App\app.exe on Windows or /usr/bin/app on Linux. SMTO needs a complete location; a bare name like "notepad" isn't enough.
  3. On a Mac, give the full location of the app (for example /Applications/Safari.app) or its exact app ID (for example com.apple.Safari). macOS finds apps only by their location or their app ID.

What success looks like

  • SMTO reports the app as started and you can see it open on that computer.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages that Gateway computer, with the name of the app you wanted to open.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Desktop launch_application found no application: no existing absolute file at the target-local path, or no macOS application for the supplied bundle identifier.

What this means

  • Launch resolution found no application for the supplied macOS identifier or no existing absolute application file at the supplied target-local path. These operations address the selected Gateway desktop. Metadata discovery does not authorize content reads, and a native control request is not proof of completed effects; retain exact operation and target identities.

Why this can happen

  • Launch resolution found no application for the supplied macOS identifier or no existing absolute application file at the supplied target-local path.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the exact bundle identifier or absolute path on the selected Gateway, rather than a similarly named controller application.

How to fix it

  • Supply an existing absolute executable path on the selected Gateway (an .exe on Windows), an existing absolute .app bundle path on macOS, or a bundle ID that NSWorkspace URLForApplicationWithBundleIdentifier resolves on that host. Relative names and PATH lookups are not supported.
  • Use an existing absolute application path or a canonical bundle ID on the selected Gateway.

Retry and execution caution

  • Use an existing absolute application path or a canonical bundle ID on the selected Gateway.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended application resolves to an existing supported target on that Gateway.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass identity protection or automatically replay an uncertain mutation.

Technical notes

  • These operations address the selected Gateway desktop. Metadata discovery does not authorize content reads, and a native control request is not proof of completed effects; retain exact operation and target identities.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
